deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It is a page of lecture or study notes on ancient Greek history, written in German Kurrent. It continues directly from the previous page (the Argonauts, the Seven against Thebes, the Trojan War) and runs into the next (the return of the Heraclidae).

Content, in order:
(a) End of the first period. The Greeks were still closely bound to one another. Their constitutions were then all monarchical. They already lived in towns, and arts, daily labour and agriculture (reading uncertain) set peace apart from war.
(b) New section heading: 'Zweiter Zeitraum. Von dem Trojanischen Krieg bis auf den Anfang der Perser Kriege, c. 1200 – 500 [BC]'. Subheading: '1. Geschichte der Hellenischen Staaten. Innerhalb Griechenland.'
(c) Thesis: the Trojan War did Greece more harm than good, for two reasons:
1. The long absence of the leaders caused great disorder in Greece.
2. At about the same time a far more important upheaval came, the Dorian migration. The text begins to explain it: the families of Heracles fled to the Dorians, who had their seat in Doris. The sentence continues on folio 56.

The content is standard textbook material of c. 1800 German Gymnasium or university teaching, in the style of A. H. L. Heeren's handbooks of ancient history. The hand and the subject suggest notes copied or taken by a student or family member, not Gauss's own mathematical work. Nothing here bears on Lagrange or mathematics despite the bundle name.
errors: Not mathematical errors. Historically, the dates given (Trojan War c. 1200 BC, Persian Wars from c. 500 BC) are the conventional ones of the era's handbooks and are unremarkable.
The next page's 'corinthischen Helden' for Heracles is presumably a mistranscription of 'griechischen'; Heracles is not Corinthian.

results.what: Periodization of Greek history: second period from the Trojan War (c. 1200 BC) to the start of the Persian Wars (c. 500 BC); consequences of the Trojan War; the Dorian migration and the Heraclidae
results.modern_name: Standard 18th/19th-century schoolbook periodization of ancient Greek history (Dorian invasion / Return of the Heraclidae)
results.usually_credited_to: Conventional; cf. A. H. L. Heeren, Handbuch der Geschichte der Staaten des Alterthums (1799)

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains only routine history lecture notes with no mathematical content. They are probably not even Gauss's own composition.

checkable.asserts: Length in years of the 'second period' (c. 1200 to 500 BC) as given in the heading.

transcription_corrections: Line 3–4: 'wohnten sie schon in Nord Land[?]' should most likely read 'wohnten sie schon in Städ-ten' (word split across the line break).
Line 4: 'Tagesarbeit und [?] unterschied[?]' is perhaps '... und Ackerbau unterschied[en sich vom]' or similar; still uncertain.
Line 1 of the heading date: 'c. 1200 [-01-] 500' is 'c. 1200 — 500'; the struck mark is just a correction of the dash or a stray 'bis'.
'Abwesenheit der Heerführer[?]' looks more like 'der Oberhäupter' or 'Heerhäupter' in the image.
'die bisher[?] in Doris' is plausible, possibly 'die bis dahin'.
'Anfang der Perser Krieg' should probably be 'Perser Kriege'.
